To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
GALergic axons make synaptic contacts with TH-immunoreactive dendrites and somata in the AN of the rat.
galanin-containing axons make synaptic contacts with tyrosine hydroxlase-immunoreative neurons in the hypothalmic arcuate nucleus of rat.
galanin-containing axons make synapses on tyrosine-hydroxylase-immuno-reactive neurons in the rat arcuate nucleus, and that these synapses might be involved in the regulation of prolactin secretion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the afferent systems regulating the activity of the TIDA neurons, and with the elucidation of the mechanisms by which these afferents modulate the activity of these neurons.
the identification and characterization of neuronal pathways involved in the control of PRL release.
the possible involvement of the GALergic system in the control of the TIDA neurons.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
GAL is a neurotransmitter/neuroregulator in the AN.
galaninergic neurons are present in the arcuate nucleus and are in synaptic apposition to TH-IR neurons, which suggests a functional relationship between these two neuronal systems.
GALergic axons synapse directly with TH-IR neurons in the AN of the male rat, and thus may be involved in the modulation of TIDA neuronal activity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the hypothalamic AN contains a population of neurons which are regulated by both GAL and dopamine.
GALergic neurons may play a role in the regulation of the TIDA neuronal system, and thus may be involved in the control of PRL secretion.
GALergic neurons synapse on the TH-containing neurons in the AN and that this synaptic connection may be involved in the control of TIDA neuronal activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
GAL may be involved in the regulation of the TIDA neurons.
the GALergic axons are likely to be the most important source of the neurotransmitter in the TIDA system.
